tasks.short: Move mail containers safely between internal collection and distribution points using handling equipment.

steps.what: Check collection requests and choose the next container movement.
Inspect handling equipment and check the planned route for hazards.
Load or attach containers and secure them within equipment limits.
Operate handling equipment to move containers to the destination.
Unload or detach containers and place them in the designated receiving area.
Record completed movements and any delivery exceptions in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.

tasks.design: Configure a collection queue in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, with fixed destinations, equipment limits and simple priority rules; the operator confirms the next movement. A short completion form reuses the movement docket and records exceptions without retyping. Physical checks, loading, movement and unloading remain with the operator; no model loop is needed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Most effort is physical. Dispatch and recording improvements alone often did not justify a separate implementation for an occasional task.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing configurable queues and forms can reduce paperwork. AI-assisted coding can lower the cost of small configuration extensions, but does not remove physical handling constraints.
tasks.still_hard: Congestion, unstable loads, pedestrians and equipment faults require situational judgement. Driverless movement would need separate equipment, site engineering and safety validation, outside this estimate.
tasks.human_edge: The operator notices unsafe loads and changing floor conditions, stops movement, and coordinates safe passage with nearby people.
tasks.altitude: The operator spends slightly less time choosing jobs and recording completion. Equipment operation dominates the task, so the week and decision rights change little.

reach.task: Review internal collection routes and receiving-area congestion.
reach.learn: Learn how pedestrian separation, access restrictions and collection windows shape safe routes.

evidence.claim: Software can simplify movement queues and records, while physical equipment operation remains site-dependent.
The proposed time shares and remaining effort are planning estimates, not measured results.
The digest documents business-mail scanning and form digitisation, but provides no evidence for automating physical container movement.
Apply GDPR to personal movement records and assess any AI component under the EU AI Act. Employee consultation requirements depend on national rules; the proposed design needs no AI component.

assumptions: This describes a company site that already uses powered handling equipment; many mid-size offices use hand trolleys instead.
Movements stay within the site and use established receiving areas.
The baseline uses paper or phone dispatch and completion entry in the {OPS_SYSTEM}.
The estimate covers queue and form configuration, not vehicles, building alterations or driverless operation.
The physical nature of the work supports the low automation prior; small administrative savings remain plausible.
unknowns: Actual equipment types, movement frequency, container volumes and current dispatch means.
Whether the {OPS_SYSTEM} supports configurable queues and mobile completion forms.
Operator qualifications, equipment limits and local traffic arrangements.
Whether movement records identify employees and how long records must be retained.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.
Whether saved administrative time justifies implementation at this task's actual frequency.
research_questions: Can existing queue and completion-form configuration meet the need without custom code?
What completion evidence can be captured with minimal operator effort?
new_work: Maintain destinations, collection windows and equipment eligibility rules.
Resolve stale requests, duplicate movements and incorrect completion entries.
Check access permissions and record retention.
Train operators on the queue and short completion form.

role.altitude: This supplemental task remains mainly physical. Administrative effort falls modestly, with no automatic increase in decision authority.
reach: Support the facilities manager with evidence about collection routes and congestion.
skills_to_grow: Safe equipment operation and load assessment
Simple digital dispatch and exception recording
role.ambitious_version: Help redesign collection rounds with the facilities manager, using aggregate movement records and direct observation of bottlenecks.

job.title: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
